name: Lonelygirl15
title: The Girl Who Fooled YouTube
claims: lonelygirl15 is an American science fiction thriller web series created by Miles Beckett, Mesh Flinders, Greg Goodfried, and Amanda Goodfried | [1]
It was independently released on YouTube from June 16, 2006, to August 1, 2008, and briefly on Revver and Myspace | [1]
The series revolves around homeschooled 16-year-old Bree Avery (Jessica Lee Rose) using the username Lonelygirl15 | [1]
Bree goes on the run with Daniel (Yousef Abu-Taleb) after her parents' religion is revealed to be The Order, a blood-harvesting operation | [1]
The series is presented through video blogs originally recorded from Bree's bedroom | [1]
Beckett, a doctor after discovering YouTube in 2005, conceived a staged video blog series with Flinders, a filmmaker | [1]
Greg and Amanda Goodfried were brought on as lawyers to handle business and manage Bree's online affairs | [1]
Bree's first vlogs were posted in June 2006 and quickly gained popularity, with users believing she was real | [1]
Lonelygirl15 was the most-subscribed YouTube channel for 226 days, surpassing geriatric1927, and first to reach 50,000 subscribers | [1]
Users found proof it was fake by messaging Bree on Myspace and tracing her IP to Creative Artists Agency | [1]
A Los Angeles Times story and a blog post by Tom Foremski revealing Rose's identity outed the hoax in September 2006 | [1]
Viewership continued to grow, experiencing its highest viewership in 2007 | [1]
Bree has been called YouTube's first viral star; the show pioneered vlogging and won a Webby Award and VH1 Big in '06 Award | [1]
EQAL produced spinoffs like KateModern and LG15: The Resistance | [1]
Season 1 features Bree, P-Monkey, and Danielbeast, building up to a mysterious ceremony involving dieting, shots, and Enochian | [1]
Lucy staged a fake ceremony for Daniel, and Bree's parents disappeared after she refused to attend a secret ceremony | [1]
Cast includes Jessica Lee Rose, Yousef Abu-Taleb, Jackson Davis, Alexandra Dreyfus, Becki Kregoski, Maxwell Glick, Katherine Pawlak, Melanie Merkosky, Crystal Young, and Raegan Payne | [1]
Beckett quit a plastic surgery program and found YouTube after seeing The Lonely Island's "Lazy Sunday" | [1]
Beckett met Flinders at The Gaslite in Santa Monica in April 2006 and wrote a script in two weeks | [1]
Flinders's character inspiration came from his Northern California commune upbringing and occult knowledge | [1]
Grant Steinfeld dropped out after helping distribute videos and create a dummy site | [1]
Casting call was posted on Craigslist as The Children of Anchor Cove, held using Film Independent space | [1]
Jessica Lee Rose graduated from the New York Film Academy and auditioned in April 2006 | [1]
Yousef Abu-Taleb worked as a Red Lobster server and was cast for his dorky look | [1]
Rose and Abu-Taleb deleted personal accounts, signed NDAs, and stayed in their houses for three months funded by creators | [1]
Katharine McPhee guest-starred in "Truth or Dare" in January 2007 | [1]
The first video "First Blog/Dorkiness Prevails" cost $130, used a broken desk lamp, Logitech QuickCam, and Flinders's bedroom | [1]
Rose unscripted/paraphrased lines; episodes took about 1 hour to film, 2-3 per day | [1]
Season 1 ended in August 2007 after 260 episodes; final 12 episodes were exclusive to MySpaceTV and Lonelygirl15.com | [1]
Bree's death was prompted by contract negotiations and Rose's request | [1]
Flinders and Goodfried went into about $50,000 of credit card debt initially | [1]
Lonelygirl15 partnered with the UN in October 2006 and signed a five-figure deal with Hershey's for Ice Breakers Sours in March 2007 | [1]
Signed a deal with Amie Street in May 2007 | [1]
